semanticHints.description: Individual physical or electronic item records (barcodes, status, call number, material type, loan type). Each item belongs to a holdings_record.
terms: MARC query with item filter performance
nested EXISTS pattern for instance-level queries with item-level filters
preferredApproach: ALWAYS access items through holdings_record_id to use the composite index. Never scan item__t first and join back to holdings.

CRITICAL TYPE CAST: item__t FK columns (holdings_record_id, effective_location_id, permanent_location_id, material_type_id) are stored as TEXT in LDP. Target table PKs are UUID. ALWAYS cast the UUID side to TEXT: hr.id::text, loc.id::text. Lookup-to-lookup joins on small reference tables (e.g. loc.library_id = lib.id, lib.campus_id = camp.id) are UUID=UUID natively — no cast needed.
For material type filtering, use the composite index: WHERE ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id AND ii.material_type_id = <uuid>.

SINGLE-PASS CTE: When the query needs item-level detail columns in output (call_number, barcode, location name) — not just instance-level (hrid, title) — use one MATERIALIZED CTE that joins item→holdings→instance→location in a single pass, collecting both filter matches and output columns. Then apply NOT EXISTS and other filters against the small CTE result. This avoids scanning item__t twice (single-pass 474K cost vs nested EXISTS + re-join 971K cost). Pattern: WITH items AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT inst.hrid, inst.title, ii.effective_call_number_components__call_number, loc.name FROM item__t ii JOIN holdings_record__t hr ON ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id::text JOIN instance__t inst ON hr.instance_id = inst.id::text JOIN location__t loc ON ii.effective_location_id = loc.id::text WHERE ...filter...) SELECT ... FROM items WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mtNNN m WHERE m.instance_hrid = items.instance_hrid);
There is NO index on effective_location_id. For location-based queries, scope through holdings permanent_location_id first, then check items.
Use inventory.item__t for current item status and availability snapshots; use circulation tables for loan events.
Use nested EXISTS from holdings to items: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM inventory.item__t ii WHERE ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id AND ii.material_type_id = ...).
item__t has 10M+ rows. Available indexes: item__t_id_idx (id), item__t___id_idx (__id), idx_item_holdings_material (holdings_record_id, material_type_id).

warnings: TEXT type — target location__t.id is UUID. Cast the UUID side: ii.effective_location_id = loc.id::text
TEXT type — target holdings_record__t.id is UUID. Cast the UUID side: ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id::text
